chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Sulayman ibn Dawud (peace be upon them) that the sign of your death is a tree emerging from Bayt al-Maqdis, called Al-Kharnuba.
So Sulayman looked one day, and behold, the Al-Kharnuba tree had emerged from Bayt al-Maqdis. He said to it, 'What is your name?' It said, 'Al-Kharnuba.'
Sulayman turned back towards his prayer niche and stood in it, leaning on his staff. His soul was captured at that very moment.

The Jinn and humans continued to serve him and strive in his affairs as they had been, thinking that he was alive and had not died. They would go in the morning and return in the evening, while he stood firm.
Until the woodworm gnawed into his staff, ate through the joint, and it broke. Then Sulayman fell to the ground.

Do you not hear the statement of the Mighty and Majestic: 'And when he fell, the Jinn came to know plainly that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.'

key_terms.الْخُرْبُوبَة: Al-Kharnuba (A specific type of tree, often identified as the carob tree)
key_terms.الْغَيْب: The Unseen (knowledge of the future or hidden matters)
key_terms.مِحْرَاب: Mihrab (Prayer niche or place of worship)

ai.seo_question: What was the sign of Prophet Sulayman's death and how did the Jinn discover it?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the mechanism of the Prophet Sulayman’s (AS) death, highlighting how the Jinn remained in their labor unaware of his passing until the decay of his staff revealed the truth. It serves as a key exegetical link to Quran 34:14, illustrating the concept of *ghayb* (the unseen) and the temporary nature of prophetic signs, a theme often cited in Shia scholarship to discuss the continuity of divine authority and the nature of death for the righteous.
